cards.text: Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, have marched on Jerusalem, and King Ahaz of Judah and his people are trembling, but the LORD has already told Ahaz their plan will not happen (Isaiah 7:1-7). Now the prophet Isaiah tells what the LORD says to him next: take a large scroll and write on it with an ordinary stylus. The words to write are Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

The LORD says He will appoint trustworthy witnesses for Himself: Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberekiah. Then Isaiah says he had relations with the prophetess, and she conceives and gives birth to a son.

cards.question: Isaiah's son is born. What does the LORD tell Isaiah to name him?

answers.text: The words from the large scroll
The name of Ahaz king of Judah

cards.text: Then the LORD sets a clock on it: before the boy knows how to cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ something will happen to Damascus, where Rezin rules, and Samaria, where the son of Remaliah rules (Isaiah 7:8-9). A countdown measured in baby words, friend, and no snooze button.

cards.question: Before Isaiah's son can cry ‘Father’ or ‘Mother,’ the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be ___.

cards.text: And the one carrying it all off is the king of Assyria.

Then the LORD speaks to Isaiah again: this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah. Friend, gently flowing water is the sound people play on their phones to fall asleep, and they said NO THANKS.

cards.question: The LORD says this people, who rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, rejoiced in Rezin and the son of Remaliah.
Because this people rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah, what will the Lord bring against them?

answers.text: The mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates
A long famine in the land

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, the mighty floodwaters of the Euphrates stand for the king of Assyria and all his pomp.

cards.text: The flood will overflow its channels and overrun its banks. Gentle waters out. Floodwaters in.

cards.question: The LORD says the flood will overflow its banks and pour into ___.

cards.text: It will swirl and sweep over Judah, reaching all the way up to the neck.
And the LORD says its spreading streams will cover “your entire land, O Immanuel!” That name was in the sign the LORD gave Ahaz, a son who will be called Immanuel (Isaiah 7:14).
Then the message turns to the peoples and all the distant lands: huddle together, pay attention, prepare for battle. And “prepare for battle” comes up TWICE.

cards.question: The peoples are told to huddle together and prepare for battle, and that they will be ___.
The message goes on: devise a plan, state a proposal. It says the plan and the proposal will happen.
The message says the plan will be thwarted and the proposal will not happen. What reason does it give?

answers.text: For their kings are too weak
